intended_object: Take a quasi-compact scheme X locally of finite type over a field k, with A(X) ⊆ Γ(X, O_X) the selected (greatest finite étale) component subalgebra. For a field extension K/k, the intended object is the K-subalgebra of Γ(X_K, O) given by the image of A(X) ⊗_k K under the canonical map to Γ(X_K, O). This is the K-span of A(X) inside the global sections of the base change. I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation and the companion theorem `baseChangedComponentSubalgebra_eq`.
explanation:
The definition is the range of `componentScalarExtensionAlgHom`, which is the composite of three maps:
- the swap A(X) ⊗_k K ≅ K ⊗_k A(X);
- the scalar extension K ⊗ A(X) → K ⊗ Γ(X), which is the base change of the subalgebra inclusion `val.baseChange K`;
- the canonical flat-base-change isomorphism K ⊗_k Γ(X, O) ≅ Γ(X_K, O). Its hypotheses hold because X is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian.

So the range is exactly the image of A(X) ⊗_k K in Γ(X_K, O), as intended. This also means it is the base change of the subalgebra A(X), carried over into Γ(X_K).

Mathlib's `Subalgebra.baseChange` is the analogous construction, but its ambient ring is K ⊗ A, not Γ(X_K). The point of this definition is to place the subalgebra inside the global sections of the base-changed scheme, so that it can be compared with `componentSubalgebra (schemeBaseChange X)`. The library proves the two are equal in `baseChangedComponentSubalgebra_eq`.

The setting (fields k and K, X quasi-compact and locally of finite type) is the natural one for the π₀ / component algebra, so the definition is not too narrow. Although it is an intermediate object in the proof, it is a meaningful, publicly exported subalgebra and it is defined correctly.
